core_idea: New DNA analysis has revealed that a richly buried Iron Age leader, long presumed to be a male 'Celtic Prince,' was in fact female, forcing a re-evaluation of ancient power structures.
video_title: The Iron Age King Who Was Actually a Queen? DNA Rewrites History!
script: What if everything we thought we knew about an ancient king was wrong? For decades, archaeologists believed they'd found the tomb of a powerful Iron Age leader in Germany. Buried with riches, weapons, and even chariots, it was a textbook example of ancient male authority. But new DNA analysis of the skeletal remains just dropped a bombshell. The individual, previously identified as "The Celtic Prince," was definitively female. This isn't just about changing a name. It challenges our entire understanding of gender roles and power in the Iron Age. A woman commanding such respect, wealth, and military symbols? It's revolutionary. This discovery forces us to re-examine history through a new lens, proving the past is far more complex and surprising than we ever imagined.
